# Sati-RCA v0 — results on real fault-injection data

Trained and tested on **RCAEval** (phamquiluan/RCAEval @ `afeacb11bcc9`), 735 real fault-injection cases on three microservice systems. Model `sati-rca-v0`, sha256 `f0e8103c20ac04d3…`. Root cause absent from the candidate services in 0 case(s) — counted as misses.

AC@k is the share of incidents whose true root-cause service is ranked in the top k; Avg@5 is the mean of AC@1–AC@5 (RCAEval's headline). Brackets are Wilson 95% intervals. **Baseline** ranks services by their largest robust shift, with no learning — the number a model has to beat to be worth being a model.

## Ablation — without the series-count feature

`n_series` counts a service's metrics. RCAEval's root causes are always application services, which tend to carry more series than databases, so a model can lean on *which kind of service* rather than *what changed*. Leave-one-system-out without it:

| Features | AC@1 | AC@3 | Avg@5 | n |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| all | 88.4 (85.7–90.6) | 96.9 (95.3–98.0) | 95.3 | 645 |
| without `n_series` | 88.5 (85.8–90.8) | 97.0 (95.5–98.1) | 95.3 | 645 |

## How to read this

- The leave-one-system-out rows are the claim. The repetition rows are in-distribution and will look better; the gap between them is how much of the score is memory of a system.
- Fault-type accuracy is end to end: it is scored on the service Sati-RCA ranked first, so a wrong root cause is also a wrong fault.
- These models were designed, written and trained by an AI assistant (Claude) under the owner's direction ([adr/RealDataModels](../../adr/RealDataModels.md)).
